meta: Mary Magdalene at her dressing table while her sister Martha urges her to repent: Jan van Troyen's 1660 print after a painting in Vienna.
about: Mary Magdalene sits at a dressing table while her hair is being done. Her sister Martha stands at the left and points out her vanity, hoping to bring her back to repentance. Jan van Troyen engraved the scene after a painting by Lupicini that hangs in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna. David Teniers probably painted a small oil study of each picture in the collection of Archduke Leopold Wilhelm, and these served as models for the printmakers. The Rijksmuseum notes that it is not always clear whether Teniers or his workshop made them.

meta: Joseph with his bow and Benjamin beside a wolf and a sheep: Johann Sadeler's 1585 engraving of two sons of Jacob, kept in an album.
about: Two brothers stand side by side, each labelled with his name. Joseph holds a bow and pulls an arrow from the quiver on his back. Next to Benjamin a wolf devours a sheep, an allusion to Benjamin as a ravening wolf. Below the figures a Latin line points to the biblical passage. Johann Sadeler made the engraving in 1585. It is now part of an album in the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Minerva enthroned on clouds with putti and the arts around her: Pieter Sluyter's 1693 engraving of a ceiling piece.
about: Minerva sits enthroned on the clouds in helmet and armour, with spear and shield at her side. Putti around her hold the attributes of the arts and the sciences. Far behind her Jupiter clutches his head, a nod to the myth that Minerva was born from it. The subject is a ceiling piece. Pieter Sluyter made the print in 1693, and it is now bound into an album.

meta: A flower-decked carriage and mounted musicians in the 1872 Haarlem procession: plate three of twelve, published by Emrik and Binger.
about: A carriage covered in flowers carries seated women draped in garlands, with mounted musicians and a banner bearer in period dress riding alongside. The parade was held in Haarlem on 1 April 1872, during the April festivities that marked 300 years of Dutch independence. This is the third of twelve sheets pasted together into one long strip. It covers the groups numbered 13 to 16. Emrik & Binger made the series. Plate three of twelve.

meta: Minister Heemskerk as the Easter ox: Johan Michaël Schmidt Crans's 1888 caricature for De Nederlandsche Spectator.
about: A decorated ox is led through a church while several men look on, and its garland is lettered Ministerie Heemskerk. The cartoon turns the minister into the Easter ox of its title, De Paaschos van Staat. Johan Michaël Schmidt Crans drew it for the weekly De Nederlandsche Spectator, where it appeared as number 13 in 1888. A verse runs beneath the scene.

meta: Felix Hess's 1910 caricature of finance minister Kolkman as an alchemist in his workshop, printed as a supplement to a weekly.
about: A bearded man works in a laboratory over a retort and distilling apparatus, and the labels on the equipment are tax terms such as Budget 1911 and New Taxes. Felix Hess drew the cartoon to show the finance minister Kolkman as an alchemist. It came out as a supplement to De Nieuwe Amsterdammer of 28 October 1910, number 7. The Rijksmuseum lists it as not in Frederik Muller.

meta: A pharmacist of the Dutch Medical Service in uniform: Willem Charles Magnenat's hand-coloured lithograph from an 1845 uniform book.
about: A man in a blue jacket with red trim and grey trousers stands in a garden holding a cocked hat. Behind him a second figure in the same blue stands near a statue. The sheet is a hand-coloured lithograph of the uniform worn by pharmacists in the Medical Service. Willem Charles Magnenat made it as an illustration for a book of 1845 on the uniforms and clothing of the Dutch army, navy and civic guards, including those in the overseas territories.

meta: Daffodils and primroses in Gerard Valck's flower print from about 1670, number 60 in a bound series.
about: Several daffodil blooms rise on long stems above strap-like leaves, with clusters of small primroses in the lower corners. The print belongs to a bound, numbered series of eleven flower prints. The set probably had twelve at first. Its series number is 60, and the imprint names Gerard Valck of Amsterdam as publisher. Gerard Valck's engraving is dated 1670.

meta: Two soldiers by a door: Heinrich Krabbé's 1898 ink drawing, marked for reproduction and annotated with a chapter title.
about: Two soldiers face each other beside a door. One leans his right knee on a chair and holds a notebook, while the other stands with a sword belt at his side. A handwritten note on the front names the chapter First Desertion in Time of Peace, gives page 29 and begins a line addressed to a quartermaster sergeant. Heinrich Krabbé drew it in 1898, and the sheet carries an instruction for making a printing block. On the back is an impression of another drawing of two standing men.

meta: A garlanded guild ox: a hand-coloured woodcut from 1848 by Lutkie and Cranenburg.
about: A white ox stands on a striped ground with garlands of flowers wound around its body and horns. A border of flower tendrils and cups frames the picture, and a two-line verse runs underneath. The sheet shows a guild ox, also called a fair ox or prize ox. Lutkie & Cranenburg made it as a woodcut coloured in blue, yellow and red in 1848, with the text in letterpress. It is numbered 55 at the top right.

meta: The Fountain of Proserpina at the Villa d'Este in Tivoli: Giovanni Francesco Venturini's 1653 print, plate 19 of an album.
about: The Fountain of Proserpina fills a niche of columns and carved reliefs, with Pluto, king of the underworld, carrying the girl off at its centre. Small figures in period dress walk the garden around it. Giovanni Francesco Venturini made the print in 1653 at Tivoli. It is numbered 19 at lower right and is now mounted in an album.

meta: Odysseus arrives on the island of the Cyclopes: Theodoor van Thulden's 1633 print, mounted in an album.
about: Odysseus lands with his men on the island of the Cyclopes. In the foreground one of his crew drinks from a dish, and next to him sits a river god with a jug. Armoured companions watch from the rocks. Theodoor van Thulden etched and engraved the scene in 1633, and the print has letterpress text below it. It is pasted onto a page of an album.

meta: The murder of Agamemnon and Cassandra at the banquet: Theodoor van Thulden's 1633 etching and engraving.
about: After his arrival in Mycenae Agamemnon is killed at the banquet by Aegisthus. Beside him Clytemnestra kills Cassandra. Furniture is overturned and soldiers with swords crowd the room, while a chariot and classical columns stand at the edges. Theodoor van Thulden made the print in 1633, and a French caption beneath describes the scene. It is pasted onto an album page.

meta: A travelling wagon outside the walls of Douai: Pieter Hendricksz. Schut's 1660 etching, part of an album.
about: A woman sits in a covered wagon pulled by one horse, with a boy riding on the horse's back. Beside the wagon walk a man with a gun over his shoulder and a woman carrying a child. Behind them rises the town of Douai, a dense skyline of church spires and rooftops behind its walls. Pieter Hendricksz. Schut etched the view in 1660. It is mounted in an album.

meta: The title page of a series on 24 female martyrs: Adriaen Collaert's engraving from about 1590.
about: A heart-shaped cartouche carries the title of a series of 24 scenes of female martyrs. Two winged angels hold garlands on either side beneath an IHS monogram, and a cherub sits below. Adriaen Collaert engraved the sheet around 1590. The pictures in the series are surrounded by borders of flowers and animals, and the Latin dedication fills the cartouche.

meta: A rider and two oxen wading the Naruko ford: Hirafuku Hyakusui's colour woodblock print of 1917.
about: A rider on a dark ox leads a second ox, loaded with bundles, through shallow water at the Naruko ford. Grey mountains rise behind them under a misty sky, and a single reddish tree stands at the right edge. The Rijksmuseum describes a man driving cattle through the shallows toward the bank at the foot of a mountain. Hirafuku Hyakusui made the colour woodblock print in 1917. The drawing is carried by a black line block, and separate blocks add the colour.

meta: Eight miracles of Christ with Dutch verses: a hand-tinted woodcut sheet of about 1725 by Monogrammist WH.
about: One sheet holds eight woodcut scenes from the Gospels about the miracles of Christ. Under each picture stands a Dutch verse, and a publisher's imprint runs along the bottom. The woodcut is tinted in blue, yellow and orange, with the text set in letterpress. It is numbered 20 at the top right. The maker signed only with a monogram, WH, so his name is unknown to the museum, and the sheet dates from 1725.

meta: The Palazzo della Cancelleria in Rome: Alessandro Specchi's 1699 view, one of 52 palace prints.
about: The long main facade of the Palazzo della Cancelleria runs across the sheet with its arcaded ground floor, and a bell tower rises beside it. Carriages, dogs and figures fill the piazza in front. A title and a numbered key to the details are engraved in the bottom margin. The print is one of 52 views of Roman palaces by Alessandro Specchi, made in 1699. Together with four other series they form the large work Il nuovo teatro di Roma moderna. It is mounted in an album.

meta: The Collegio Romano in Rome: Alessandro Specchi's 1699 print from a series of palace views.
about: Above the long facade of the Collegio Romano rises a central tower, and a row of windows runs along its side. Figures in period dress cross the foreground, and a horse-drawn carriage passes by. Title and numbered key are engraved below. Alessandro Specchi made the print in 1699 as one of 52 views of palaces in Rome. With four other series, these views form the large work Il nuovo teatro di Roma moderna. The sheet is mounted in an album.

meta: Hendrik Petrus Berlage's 1919 design for the cover of Stijn Streuvels's Genoveva van Brabant, with two coats of arms and a publisher's vignette.
about: On the front board two horizontal lines are crossed by two vertical ones, and a frame in the middle holds the title and the author's name. A coat of arms stands on each side. The left one shows a lion, the symbol of the province of Brabant, and the right one two trees on steps with a cross between them. Below the name sits the vignette of the publisher L.J. Veen. Hendrik Petrus Berlage drew the design in 1919 in ink over pencil and corrected it with white paint.

meta: History writes a book while Father Time lies fallen: Frederik Ottens's allegory of the art of writing, printed in 1727.
about: History sits on a staircase writing a book, surrounded by putti and allegorical figures. Truth sits on a cloud above her with a sun over her head, and the fallen Father Time lies on the ground among putti with books and papers. The allegory is of the art of writing. The Rijksmuseum thinks the print was probably a title page. Frederik Ottens made it in 1727. It came from a scrapbook of title prints and ornaments on blue paper, which was taken apart in 1983.

meta: Saint Thomas Aquinas girded by angels: Richard Collin's 1649 print for the Militia Angelica brotherhood founded at Leuven.
about: Saint Thomas Aquinas is girded with a chastity belt by two angels, and below, members of the brotherhood hand such belts out in the street to clergy and citizens. The print records the founding of the Militia Angelica Thomae Aquinatis on 7 March 1649. The Dominican Franciscus Deurwerders started the brotherhood at the University of Leuven. Richard Collin engraved the sheet. The ten commandments of the Militia fill the middle.

meta: Vlaardingen seen from the water: Joost van Geel's 1666 view, made for a large map of Rotterdam and its surroundings.
about: Vlaardingen is seen from the water, with the town hall at the left and the Great Church to its right. Sailing ships fill the river, and the town's coat of arms and the title sit at the top centre. Joost van Geel etched the view as part of the Maas map of 1666, a large map that also had a title strip and a big view of Rotterdam printed from six plates. The map's title says 1665, yet archive research shows it was ready a year later.

meta: A bird's-eye plan of Schoonhoven: Julius Milheuser's hand-coloured map of 1649.
about: A bird's-eye plan of Schoonhoven shows the dense street grid, church towers and the canals and fortifications around the town. The coat of arms of Holland sits at the upper left, above the dedication, a key numbered 1 to 20 and a scale bar of 30 roeden. Schoonhoven's own arms are at the upper right. Julius Milheuser made the plan in 1649 as an etching and engraving. It was coloured by hand.

meta: The kabuki actor Sawamura Sojuro III as Oda Izuminosuke, dancing with a bamboo branch: Katsukawa Shunko's woodblock print of 1787.
about: Kabuki actor Sawamura Sojuro III dances in the role of Oda Izuminosuke with a bamboo branch in his hand. His trousers have long legs that trail along the floor and a pattern of chrysanthemums. The cranes flying across the top of his costume are symbols of good luck. The print shows a scene from the play Keisei Ide no Yamabuki, staged at the Nakamura theatre on 6 June 1787. Katsukawa Shunko made it as a colour woodblock print with a black line block.

meta: Two striped tulips and a butterfly: Jacob Marrel's 1639 watercolour on parchment, with the varieties named below.
about: Two striped red and white tulips with green leaves stand side by side, and a small yellow and brown butterfly rests between them. The names of the varieties are written below in a careful hand: Sipion Victorij and General de France. Jacob Marrel painted the flowers in 1639 in watercolour and bodycolour over pencil on parchment. The sheet belongs to an album.

meta: A Ural owl on a branch: Anselmus Boetius de Boodt's 1596 drawing from an album made for Emperor Rudolf II.
about: A grey Ural owl with barred wings and tail perches on a branch before a sketched ruined wall. The Latin name is written at the top right, and a note in Dutch and French sits below. Anselmus Boëtius de Boodt painted it in 1596. It is numbered 29 in the first album of bird drawings. That is the third of twelve albums of animals, birds and plants known from around 1600, made on the orders of Emperor Rudolf II. The drawing is on loan from a private collection.

meta: The tomb of Pope Alexander VII in its niche: Alessandro Specchi's hand-coloured print of 1693, with plate and page numbers.
about: A tomb monument stands in a large arched niche, with allegorical female figures and Death below and a sculpture of Pope Alexander VII above. His coat of arms hangs over the niche. Alessandro Specchi made the print in 1693. The museum's copy was coloured by hand and set inside a yellow frame with a red edge. The numbers at the top, Tabula 36 and page 113, mark its place in a larger work. It is mounted in an album.

meta: Part seven of Cornelis Anthonisz.'s woodcut bird's-eye map of Amsterdam, from a later edition of the map first issued in 1544.
about: This sheet is the seventh part of a bird's-eye map of Amsterdam, and eleven of its twelve parts survive here. It belongs to the fourth edition, from about 1557, of De vermaerde koopstadt van Amstelredam. Six editions are known. The map was printed from twelve woodblocks that never changed, although the text block was set again or adjusted for each edition. Canals, gardens and rows of houses fill the sheet, and sailing ships lie along the waterfront.

meta: Part ten of Cornelis Anthonisz.'s woodcut bird's-eye map of Amsterdam, from a later edition of the map first issued in 1544.
about: Moored sailing ships and small rowing boats line a quay on this sheet, with rows of warehouses behind them. It is the tenth part of a bird's-eye map of Amsterdam, and the twelfth part of this set is missing. The sheet comes from the fourth edition, about 1557, of De vermaerde koopstadt van Amstelredam, a large map of the city. Six editions are known. The twelve woodblocks stayed the same throughout, while the text was set again for each edition.

meta: The star-shaped plan of Fort de Voorn, also called Fort Nassau: Nicolaes van Geelkercken's 1653 print.
about: A star-shaped fortification plan shows the bastions of Fort de Voorn, also called Fort Nassau, and the moats around it. A river labelled De Maes runs along the lower edge. Nicolaes van Geelkercken made the print in 1653. It first appeared in Arend van Slichtenhorst's history of Gelderland, published at Arnhem, and was used again in a book of maps of the duchy in 1672. The plan was originally printed from a single plate together with two other plans.

meta: Apollo rewards the arts and sciences while Minerva crowns the genius of France: Simon Henri Thomassin's 1711 engraving.
about: Gods, goddesses and putti gather on clouds inside an ornate architectural frame with scrolling cartouches. Apollo hands out rewards to the sciences and arts, while Minerva crowns the genius of France. Simon Henri Thomassin engraved the scene in 1711. The painting it reproduces is by Pierre Mignard, and the Rijksmuseum records it as a ceiling painting at Versailles.

meta: Emperor Charles V consults the architects of the monastery he is having built: Cornelis Boel's print of 1614, one of eight triumphs.
about: Charles V, crowned with laurel, speaks with the architects of the monastery he has ordered to be built. One of them unrolls a plan while armoured soldiers and a horse wait nearby. Behind them workmen climb scaffolding and ladders, and the scene is dated 1555. Four lines of Latin run below. Cornelis Boel made the print in 1614 as one of a series of eight, each showing a triumph of Charles V. It is on loan from the City of Amsterdam.
